quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people walking across the street in front of you. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane after passing, make sure you have enough space between you and the other vehicle. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the water or moisture and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers (signal workers) at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers (signal workers) at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must follow flaggers' signals at construction sites. Flaggers are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, check the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, check the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks side by side, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles moving into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers of your move. Make sure the space is clear before changing lanes.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn until the light turns green.
May turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or sirens approaches you on a one-way street, you must drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road ahead in a work zone.
Children are playing ahead.
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road ahead in a work zone.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through the work zone.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop at every red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: What is true about larger vehicles?

options.text: They have larger blind spots.
They have smaller blind spots.
They have no blind spots.
They have the same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead and pull in front of the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Cyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can cause the cyclist to lose control.

questions.question: Under good driving conditions, what is the minimum following distance between your vehicle and the one in front?

options.text: Two seconds.
Four seconds.
Six seconds.
Eight seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you under ideal driving conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates drivers behind you and causes them to make unsafe passing moves. Drive with the flow of traffic at the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or passing, signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes only when necessary. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not immediately brake. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
A driver may turn in the direction the arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must make a complete stop. Wait until the light changes to green or a green arrow appears before you go. Unless a sign says otherwise, you cannot proceed.

questions.question: If your car loses traction on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Brake firmly to prevent your car from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When you lose traction on wet roads, your tires may ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. Slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right. Slow to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway begins. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right. Slow to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right. Slow to the speed indicated on the sign (in this case, 35 mph).

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
It means the same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must make a complete stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic is merging from the right.
The highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic from the right is merging into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
The right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending. Drivers in that lane must merge to another lane.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Go slower.
Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road with traffic backed up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when you must.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: In both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: If another car might hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks where people cross the road. Watch for pedestrians crossing here.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and go carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for traffic crossing, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop as you go faster. When driving at high speeds, look far ahead so you have time to react to danger safely.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
You may see more pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown. An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive slower.
Stay farther back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly, and following too close is dangerous for you and the rider. If the rider falls, you need space to avoid them. Falls are most likely on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or railroad tracks.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass it.
You may not be able to legally pass it.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching one from behind. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or other property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle or property.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:

options.text: A deaf person.
A person involved with a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians.
Speed up as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let any traffic and pedestrians still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
The railroad crossing is in a city with frequent trains.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time from either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them with one mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: You must always obey school crossing guards near schools.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Always check mirrors and signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: A bad suspension system can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle. If your car bounces too much after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You are in a minor crash at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
